candidate: Little Rock/Tyrone USNR cover test plots

measured_cover_evidence.measurement_method: five test pits distributed across the test plot area
treatment_variables: mulch applied before versus after seeding

fatal_blocker: The four approximately half-acre treatments were designed to compare seed mixes and mulch timing, not cover depth. The as-built report states that all five thickness test pits exceeded the same 36-inch minimum and measured 38 to 45 inches. Those scattered measurements do not define two exact shallow and deep polygons. Each treatment is also too small and slope-dominated to retain an independent 30-40 m clean interior after exclusions.
key_evidence: The total test plot is approximately two acres and contains four approximately half-acre treatments.
The treatment variables are seed mix and timing of mulching.
Final surveyed slope lengths are approximately 150 to 180 feet with 3:1 to 4:1 gradients.
Five test pits measured cover thicknesses ranging from 38 to 45 inches; all exceeded one common 36-inch requirement.
The public reports do not assign different measured cover depths to the four treatment polygons.
The 2020 report describes the soil surfaces as stable, but stability cannot rescue the missing depth contrast and undersized treatment geometry.
next_action: Continue the approved search for full-scale vegetated zones intentionally constructed at different measured depths, with coordinate-tied polygons, numerical uncertainty, and at least 30-40 m clean interiors.
